newsitem.title: FRANCE: Saudi barley offers seen above $150/tonne.
newsitem.headline: Saudi barley offers seen above $150/tonne.

text.p: Grain traders on Tuesday awaited results of a stop-gap Saudi barley tender expected to provide potential business for the European Union, Canada and possibly Turkey, industry sources said.
They said around four offers to supply 500,000 tonnes of optional-origin barley in late April and May went in at just above $150 per tonne, including freight.
That would pitch European Union barley around $130 per tonne, Fob, they said.

Saudi Arabia tendered on Tuesday for 500,000 tonnes of optional-origin barley with 100,000 tonnes slated for the second half of April, 150,000 tonnes for the first half of May and 250,000 tonnes in the second half of May.
Although the market had been waiting for Riyadh in May, this week's tender was mostly seen as a stop-gap measure ahead of the Eid Al-Adha religious holiday.
The two-week holiday is tentatively set to start in Saudi Arabia on April 13.
"They obviously saw a short-term gap and decided to complete their supplies until the end of May now," a European trade source said.
European traders said they expected a purchase decision by late on Wednesday. Offers had been opened and negotiations begun, they said.

Potential suppliers included the European Union, the world's top exporter with ample scope for export from its open market during the remainder of the season, traders and EU member country officials said.
"There will be some EU barley simply because of the prompt delivery dates requested by the Saudis," one exporter said.

Other possible candidates included Canada and Turkey, although some traders noted Turkey had cancelled an export tender in February and could mainly interest exporters as a bargaining chip to lean on the EU to increase export subsidies.
